Reporting Scope and Boundary
This Report covers the period from April 1, 2025, to March 31, 2026. It includes both financial and non-financial 
information for all business operations and subsidiaries/joint ventures of Lumax Auto Technologies Limited. Unless 
otherwise stated, all data is consolidated. It offers a comprehensive view through key sections such as the Board’s 
Report, Management Discussion and Analysis (MD&A), Corporate Governance Report, Business Responsibility and 
Sustainability Report (BRSR), Standalone and Consolidated Financial Statements, Auditors’ Report and the Notice of 
Annual General Meeting (AGM).
Target Audience
The Report is intended for a wide range of stakeholders, including shareholders, investors, customers, employees, 
partners, regulators and the broader community.
Our Approach to Materiality
We have identified and prioritised material topics that are most relevant to our business and stakeholders. These 
are based on industry trends, stakeholder expectations and their potential impact on our long-term performance.
Reporting Framework
The Report follows the principles of Integrated Reporting as outlined by the International Integrated Reporting 
Council (IIRC). It is prepared in line with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) (Listing Obligations and 
Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 and complies with applicable regulatory and reporting standards, 
including the Companies Act, 2013, Indian Accounting Standards (Ind-AS).

About Lumax Group
Eight Decades Strong,  
Shaping the Future of Mobility.
For over eight decades, the Lumax Group has been an integral part of India’s 
automotive journey. Established in 1945 as Globe Auto, Lumax has pioneered 
automotive lighting manufacturing. The Company has grown into a technology 
driven mobility solutions provider. Today, the Group stands as a trusted partner to 
virtually every major OEM in India, with a reputation built on innovation, scale and 
enduring relationships.
Scale and Presence
The Lumax Group operates one of the most extensive 
automotive ecosystems in India, with 40 advanced 
manufacturing facilities across eight states and overseas 
presence in Japan and China. Seven Engineering, Tech & 
Design Centres in India, Taiwan and the Czech Republic drive 
innovation, while a workforce of over 15,000 powers execution. 
OEM Relationships
Lumax has long-standing partnerships with leading automotive 
OEMs in India, including Maruti Suzuki, Hero MotoCorp, 
Honda, Mahindra & Mahindra, Tata Motors, Toyota, TVS, Royal 
Enfield and Ashok Leyland among others. Built on trust, close 
collaboration and responsive engineering support, these 
relationships reinforce Lumax Group’s position as a preferred 
partner for OEMs.
Technology Prowess
From its foundation in lighting, Lumax Group has evolved into 
a multidisciplinary technological ecosystem. The Group has 
expertise across a wide range of automotive technologies, 
including intelligent lighting, electronics, mechatronics, telematics, 
advanced plastics, vehicle structures, control systems, alternative 
fuel and emission technologies and aftermarket solutions. This 
broad capability enables Lumax to position as a Tier 0.5 partner, 
delivering integrated solutions for passenger vehicles, two-
wheelers, commercial vehicles and electric vehicles.
Legacy of Trust and Innovation
Lumax’s journey reflects resilience, foresight, and a relentless 
drive to shape the future of mobility. Guided by the ethos of its 
founder, Late Sh. S. C. Jain, and carried forward by successive 
generations, the Group has consistently anticipated industry 
shifts, from lighting to electronics, mechatronics and  
software-defined mobility. Its customer-first approach, built on 
respect, integrity, passion and excellence, continues to define 
every milestone, from the first lighting plant in Faridabad to 
today’s facilities that are progressing towards RE100.
Lumax Auto Technologies Limited

Lumax Auto Technologies Limited is a Tier-1 automotive systems manufacturer 
with a product scope that a few peers in India can match. From advanced plastics 
and vehicle interior systems to gear shifters, sensors and switches, oxygen 
sensors, telematics, CNG fuel components, the Company has built its breadth 
deliberately, through partnerships and joint ventures, each chosen for the specific 
know how it brings to the portfolio.
About the Company
Engineered for  
the Upshift.
Two Decades of Transformation:  
Our Journey from 2005 to 2025
Our growth over the last twenty years has been more than a change in scale. We have evolved from 
a component manufacturer into a diversified integrated solutions provider that continues to focus on 
moving up the value chain.
From Growth to Scale
In 2005, we were a nearly ₹ 100 Crore company focused primarily on lighting. Today, we have achieved a 
49x revenue leap to ₹ 4,870 Crore, reflecting our relentless pursuit of market leadership.
From Product to Portfolio
We have expanded from a limited product focus into a diverse portfolio, including Advanced Plastics, 
Mechatronics, Structures and Control Systems, Alternate Fuels and Aftermarket.
From Local to Pan-India
Our manufacturing presence has grown from a solitary plant to 28 state-of-the-art facilities strategically 
located in major automotive hubs. This allows us to maintain a supply chain that is responsive, cost-
efficient and technology-integrated.
From Execution to Innovation
Our engineering strength has matured to a powerhouse of over 500 R&D specialists. We have shifted our 
focus from ‘built-to-print’ to a ‘culture of innovation’.
From Niche to Universal
From serving primarily the 2-Wheeler category, we now cater to a healthy mix of Passenger Cars, 
2-Wheelers and Commercial Vehicles, ensuring we are a vital partner to every segment of the industry.
Lumax Auto Technologies Limited

Optimization of Structure  
In February 2026, the merger of Greenfuel Energy Solutions 
Private Limited with the SPV company, Lumax Resources Private 
Limited was effected. In March 2026, Lumax Ancillary Limited (LAL) 
was also merged with Lumax Auto Technologies Limited. These 
initiatives support sharper execution, improved scalability, stronger 
alignment across businesses, while enabling the Company to drive 
long-term value creation for all stakeholders.
2
Shaping Tomorrow’s Core  
In October 2025, we inaugurated the SHIFT (Smart Hub for 
Innovation and Future Trends) Tech Centre in Bengaluru, marking 
a significant step in building our in-house software and electronics 
capabilities. This facility will enable us to develop the digital 
intelligence and electronic architectures that increasingly define 
modern vehicles.
1
Full Ownership of IAC  
In May 2025, we completed the acquisition of the remaining 
25% stake in IAC International Automotive India Private Limited 
(IAC India). Subsequently IAC India was merged with Lumax Auto 
Technologies Limited. The merger enables us to integrate our 
product portfolio with interior solutions, creating a comprehensive 
value proposition for customers.
4
Portfolio Realignment  
Subsequent to the year, the Company has divested its entire 50% 
equity stake in Lumax Jopp Allied Technologies Private Limited 
(LJAT), to Jopp Holding GmbH, Germany, the Joint Venture Partner 
and acquired remaining equity stake of 15.97% in Lumax FAE 
Technologies Private Limited (LFAE) from Francisco Albero S.A.U., 
the then existing shareholder. This portfolio realignment reflects our 
continued focus on the Northstar vision and Mid-term plan  
(FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31), enabling sharper focus on businesses 
that are more closely aligned with our future growth and 
financial priorities.

Product Portfolio
Engineered for  
Every Gear.
LATL’s product portfolio is the clearest expression of the BRIDGE strategy 
in action (Bold Roadmap Integrating Diverse Growth Engines). Structured 
across five verticals - Advanced Plastics, Mechatronics, Structures and Control 
Systems, Alternate Fuels and Aftermarket - it ensures the Company has a 
relevant, technologically current offering across every major function of the 
modern vehicle.
Advanced Plastics Consistently delivering strong growth, this division is driven by OEM demands for 
sophisticated design, durability and lightweighting.

systems

Premium Interior Systems

OEMs. IAC India provides Integrated Cockpit Solutions, 
including Instrument Panels, Centre Consoles,  Door Panels,

vehicle platforms.

The Upshift in Motion.

Dear Shareholders,
Welcome to a defining moment in the 
history of Lumax Auto Technologies 
Limited (LATL).
As we present the Integrated Annual 
Report for FY 2025-26, we have chosen 
the theme ‘The Defining Upshift.’ But what 
does an 'upshift' truly mean for LATL?
In automotive terms, an upshift is a 
deliberate gear change required to handle 
greater speed, navigate new terrains and 
unlock the engine's peak performance. For 
our organization, it signifies a fundamental 
re-engineering of our corporate DNA. The 
reason behind this shift is clear: the global 
automotive landscape is undergoing a 
once-in-a-century metamorphosis. To 
survive, one might simply adapt; but to 
lead, one must transform. ‘A Defining 
Upshift’ is our leap from a traditional, 
hardware-centric Tier-1 components 
manufacturer to a technology-led, Tier-0.5 
systems integrator capable of delivering 
complex hardware-software solutions. It is 
the culmination of our two-decade journey 
from a lighting business in 2005 to a  
₹ 4,870 Crore diversified 
powerhouse today.
The Macroeconomic 
Canvas:  
Global Resilience and 
India's Rise
To truly appreciate the magnitude of our 
performance this year, it must be viewed 
against the backdrop of the broader 
macroeconomic environment.
In FY 2025-26, the global economy 
demonstrated cautious resilience. 
While inflationary pressures have 
largely cooled and central banks have 
pivoted toward growth-oriented policies, 
geopolitical fragmentation continues to 
fundamentally rewire global supply chains. 
Global OEMs are increasingly prioritizing 
‘China +1’ strategies, seeking resilient, 
diversified and high-quality manufacturing 
hubs. This realignment presents an 
unprecedented structural opportunity for 
capable global suppliers.
Amidst global realignments, India 
stands out as a formidable beacon of 
macroeconomic stability. Propelled by 
robust domestic consumption, sustained 
government capital expenditure on 
infrastructure and manufacturing schemes, 
India remains one of the fastest-growing 
major economies. Furthermore, a 
burgeoning middle class with rising 
disposable incomes is structurally altering 
consumption patterns, shifting demand 
from basic utility to premium, technology-
rich experiences.
Automotive Industry 
Trends & Macro Enablers
This robust economic momentum is 
the primary engine driving the Indian 
automotive sector. We are capitalizing on 
three highly distinct macro enablers that 
are reshaping the mobility ecosystem:
1.
 The Premiumization 
Wave 
There is a decisive consumer shift 
toward premium vehicles and SUVs 
across all segments. This is driving an 
exponential increase in the demand for 
sophisticated vehicle interiors, ambient 
lighting and advanced mechatronics.
2.
 Software-Defined V
ehicles (SDVs) 
The era of the mechanical car is giving 
way to the intelligent vehicle. The core 
value of mobility is increasingly dictated 
by connected capabilities, sensors, 
telematics and embedded electronics.
3.
 The Clean Mobility Pivot
 
Driven by stringent regulatory 
mandates and consumer awareness, 
there is a rapid acceleration towards 
sustainable transit, encompassing both 
Electric Vehicles (EVs) and Alternate 
Fuels (CNG/Hydrogen).
Performance Overview: A 
Y ear of Historic Highs
The results in FY 2025-26 have been 
nothing short of historic.
Guided by disciplined execution, we 
successfully revised our revenue growth 
y-o-y guidance twice, moving from an 
initial 20% to 25% and finally to nearly 
35%. We achieved record full-year revenue 
of ₹ 4,870 Crore. More importantly, this 
top-line scale was matched by progressive 
profitability. Our EBITDA margins 
demonstrated a consistent upward 
trajectory throughout the year, achieving a 
historic full-year margin of 14.5%, keeping 
us firmly on track to achieve our mid-term 
targets. This robust financial stability 
was further validated by CRISIL, which 
upgraded our rating to CRISIL AA with 
Stable outlook.

A Future-Ready

Aftermarket Focus
The Aftermarket segment remains a 
vital growth engine for the Company, 
consistently outperforming broader 
industry trends through a strategic 
transition toward a demand-led growth 
model. This strategy prioritizes generating 
secondary market pull by shifting focus 
from traditional channel partners to direct 
engagement with retailers and mechanics. 
This transformation is supported by an 
aggressive product expansion strategy, 
the introduction of innovative offerings 
and continuous strengthening of the 
distribution network and internal teams. 
We maintain an optimistic long-term 
outlook, expecting to build upon current 
traction through enhanced customer 
acceptance and new initiatives. As a high-
margin business, the Aftermarket segment 
is positioned to remain significantly 
margin-accretive to the Company’s 
overall performance.
Strategic Evolution: 
Architecting the Upshift

domain-level integration, systems 
thinking and software-hardware co-
development converge. 
2.
 China R

as a strategic resource for technology

Strategic Priorities for the 
Road Ahead
To maintain our industry-leading 
momentum and ensure sustainable 
value creation, our management team 
remains relentlessly focused on four 
strategic priorities:
1.
 Accelerating 
the Tier-0.5 Transition: 
Leveraging the SHIFT tech centre 
to embed proprietary software into 
the mechatronics and telematics 
portfolio, further integrating with 
interior solutions, thereby increasing 
our content per vehicle and offering 
integrated, plug-and-play systems 
directly to OEMs. 
2. Driving Premiumization 
& Localization 
Utilizing our China Resource Centre 
to scout global trends in interior cabin 
spaces and ambient lighting along with 
rapidly localizing these technologies 
to provide cost-competitive, premium 
solutions to our Indian customers.
3.
 Expanding 
the Clean 
Mobility Footprint 
Scaling Greenfuel Energy Solutions 
to dominate the alternate fuels 
(CNG/Hydrogen) and EV component 
markets, ensuring our portfolio 
remains at the absolute forefront 
of the national transition toward 
sustainable transit.
4.  Operational Synergy & 
Capital Efficiency: 
The consolidation of IAC - Intelligent 
Ambient Comfort division will 
strengthen our strategic vision and 
drive synergies by providing integrated 
solutions across lighting, plastics and 
interiors. This integration will also 
allow for better cost optimization and 
rationalization of resources, providing 
financial flexibility. Commissioning our 
Mega Mechatronics Plant at Manesar 
to seamlessly consolidate our JVs. 
These will drive significant economies 
of scale and operational synergies. 
Governance, Sustainability 
and Our ‘North Star’ Vision
As we scale rapidly, we remain anchored 
by the values that have sustained this 
Group since 1981: Respect, Integrity, 
Passion and Excellence. Our Board 
ensures that our growth is disciplined, 
transparent and ethically governed. We are 
actively decoupling our financial success 
from our environmental footprint, while the 
Lumax Charitable Foundation continues to 
invest deeply in the communities that host 
our 28 manufacturing facilities.
Looking ahead, our long-term compass 
remains our 20.20.20.20 vision: aiming 
for a 20% revenue CAGR (FY 2024-25 to 
FY 2030-31) and inching closer to 20% 
EBITDA margin over the next 5-7 years. 
By FY 2030-31, we aspire to more than 
double our current revenue base to 
upwards of ₹ 10,000 Crore, fueled by a 
blend of organic excellence and strategic 
inorganic opportunities.
We take this opportunity to express 
our deepest gratitude to you - our 
shareholders, OEM customers, joint 
venture partners and our incredibly 
dedicated workforce. FY 2025-26 has 
proven that we are not just growing with 
the industry; we are actively helping to 
elevate it.
Together, we are engineered for 
the upshift.
Warm Regards,

Materiality Assessment
Priorities Accentuated.
LATL’s materiality assessment is the mechanism through which external 
stakeholder expectations are translated into internal strategic priorities. In 
FY 2025-26, this process was conducted against a new structure with IAC - 
Intelligent Ambient Comfort division fully consolidated. The assessment tested 
whether the Company’s 16 material topics remained relevant to this expanded 
operating scope and confirmed that they do, while sharpening the urgency 
of several, particularly data security, energy management and sustainable 
procurement, in light of the new capability profile.
Lumax Auto Technologies Limited
24


--- page 28 ---
Our Materiality Assessment Process
LATL follows a structured, four-step methodology to identify and prioritise the issues most critical to 
business resilience and stakeholder trust.
Identification  
A comprehensive scan of the 
macroeconomic environment, automotive 
industry megatrends, peer disclosures 
and global ESG frameworks to compile a 
baseline list of potential material topics.
Stakeholder Engagement 
Qualitative and quantitative feedback 
is gathered from key constituents, 
including OEMs, joint venture partners, 
employees, suppliers and investors.
Prioritization  
Identified topics are evaluated across 
two dimensions: Importance to 
Stakeholders and Impact on Business 
Operations. This evaluation produces 
the Materiality Matrix.
Validation  
The prioritized list is reviewed 
and validated by the Executive 
Leadership Team and the Board 
of Directors to ensure alignment 
with corporate strategy and the risk 
management framework.

Manufactured Capital
Twenty Eight Facilities.  
The Manufacturing 
Prowess.
Twenty eight manufacturing facilities, located across India's major 
automotive hubs, form the physical foundation of LATL's upshift. The 
evolution from a single plant in 2005 to an interconnected network 
of over 28 facilities is not simply a story of growth; it is a story of 
deliberate capability expansion, each addition chosen to serve a 
specific customer cluster, a specific product vertical or a specific 
technology requirement. 
These facilities are configured for complexity, designed to deliver advanced mechatronics, premium interior systems and 
alternate fuel solutions at the quality and scale that a Tier-0.5 systems integrator must consistently demonstrate.
Our manufacturing footprint is deliberately 
structured around the principle of 
‘Customer Proximity.’ By embedding our 
facilities within or adjacent to India’s major 
automotive hubs, we ensure a resilient, 
cost-efficient and highly responsive 
supply chain.

Y okowo, Lumax Alps Alpine, Lumax Ituran and Lumax FAE. It

management control rooms, providing us with complete 
backward integration for our electronic and sensor 
product lines.

foundation of advanced software integration, electronic development and strategic global intelligence forms the 
intelligent core of our operations, enabling us to engineer comprehensive mobility solutions under the BRIDGE 
strategic framework.

Strategic Value Creation  
We manage and deploy our Intellectual Capital to stay ahead of the 
technology curve, focusing on four strategic pillars of innovation:
SHIFT 
Smart Hub for Innovation and Future Trends
In late 2025, we inaugurated our intellectual hub: the 
SHIFT tech centre in Bengaluru. Designed to accelerate 
product innovation in embedded electronics, software 
integration and connected systems, SHIFT bridges the gap 
between our hardware components and digital capabilities. 
SHIFT operates as an accelerated proof-of-concept engine 
with localization-as-differentiation approach. Global 
technology always existed, however SHIFT is working to 
make that available at scale, at optimized cost structures 
with India-specific use cases and production-ready 
solutions built here.
SHIFT’s integration of SDV principles into the mechatronics 
and telematics portfolio is organized around the principle 
that hardware-software boundary in every domain must 
become a design decision, not an accident of legacy. This 
means rearchitecting how our products are conceived 
from the ground up and not wrapping software around 
existing designs.
Our technology roadmap involves around various products 
being integrated into a systems offering. Looking ahead, 
our clean mobility pipeline is structured to ensure that 
as each regulatory milestone comes into force, LATL can 
adapt existing products and deploy platforms already 
validated at the PoC stage. The pipeline is timed to the 
policy calendar.
At SHIFT we look forward to collaborate with academia 
with an intent to upskill the ecosystem.
Proprietary & Localized Technologies
Our intellectual capital is powerfully manifested in our 
ability to indigenize complex technologies that were 
previously imported:
Strategic Technology Scouting 
The China Resource Centre
To stay ahead of global trends, we operationalized our 
office in China in early 2026. This resource center is 
dedicated to technology scouting and benchmarking, with a 
specific focus on the advanced interior cabin space trends 
emerging in the Chinese market. Beyond trend-spotting, 
this facility allows us to continuously optimize our sourcing 
and tooling for new products, ensuring we bring the latest 
technological advancements and the best value for the 
Indian market.

ESG
Sustainability as a  
Strategic Pivot.
At LATL, the same discipline that drives operational performance governs how 
the Company manages its environmental, social and governance responsibilities. 
In FY 2025-26, that discipline produced measurable outcomes: 57% renewable 
energy secured through Power Purchase Agreement Approval with the baseline 
of FY 2023-24, a real-time ESG digital dashboard deployed across the Group and 
TISAX certification achieved at LCAT. 
ESG Strategy
LATL’s ESG strategy is not a standalone 
program. It is the sustainability dimension 
of the BRIDGE framework, operating in 
parallel with the commercial, operational 
and technology engines that define 
the mid-term plan. A company that is 
upshifting its capabilities, must also upshift 
its environmental, social and governance 
performance, else the growth it achieves 
will not be durable.
The strategy is structured around  
4 pillars and 16 focus areas. Environmental 
Resilience covers energy, waste and water. 
Workforce Synergy covers occupational 
health and safety, employee wellbeing 
and diversity. Business Outreach covers 
customer satisfaction, research and 
development and corporate social 
responsibility. Sustainable Business 
Practices covers code of conduct, 
regulatory compliance, risk management, 
data security and sustainable procurement.
Against each focus area, three-year targets 
have been set and progress is tracked and 
reported. Sustainable procurement has 
been tightened to reflect the expanded 
supplier base brought in through IAC - 
Intelligent Ambient Comfort Division and 
Lumax Greenfuel. Management targets 
have been updated to reflect the 57% 
renewable energy milestone achieved 
during the year.

intent into operational action.

Strategic Value Creation  
We actively deploy our Natural Capital to drive operational 
efficiency, reduce baseline emissions and champion a circular 
economy across our 28 facilities. To better understand, track and 
mitigate our environmental impact, we measure our greenhouse 
gas (GHG) emissions strictly in accordance with the globally 
recognized WRI Greenhouse Gas Protocol.
Accelerating the Clean Energy Transition
We are systematically reducing our reliance on 
conventional fossil-fuel energy grids through robust 
energy conservation and efficiency initiatives. These 
include optimizing equipment and process operations by 
retrofitting legacy machinery with energy-efficient drives, 
upgrading to highly efficient HVAC systems, improving 
ambient air and water management and enhancing shop-
floor automation to eliminate idle power draw.
Our commitment to renewable energy is substantial and 
verifiable. Rooftop solar plants across twelve of our highest-
consuming facilities generated an impressive   
6.27 million kWh of clean energy and 2 plants in Group 
Captive (Long Term Open Access), generating a staggering  
10.26 million kWh of clean energy in FY 2025-26, effectively 
avoiding a combined 11,729.2 tCO2e of emissions. We are 
working aggressively to surpass these benchmarks in  
FY 2026-27 by identifying additional roof spaces 
and evaluating long-term off-site renewable 
power arrangements.
Circular Economy & Waste Optimization
In our Advanced Plastics and Mechatronics divisions, 
material efficiency is not just an environmental goal; it is 
a core operational KPI that directly drives profitability. We 
maintain a steadfast commitment to our target of zero waste 
to landfill, ensuring that all manufacturing by-products are 
either recycled, repurposed or safely co-processed by 
authorized partners.
Our key waste reduction initiatives are executed at a 
highly tactical, everyday level:
1
Water Stewardship & Zero Liquid  
Discharge (ZLD)
Given the water-intensive nature of certain surface 
treatment and manufacturing processes, we view water as 
a precious shared resource, particularly in regions prone 
to water scarcity. We have comprehensively upgraded 
our Sewage Treatment Plants (STP) for maximum water 
reuse and installed water-efficient fixtures across all 
administrative and shop-floor washrooms. Our operations 
now leverage smart cooling towers that optimize 
evaporation cycles, the systematic reuse of RO reject 
water for secondary applications and real-time monitoring 
to prevent subterranean leaks, ensuring we absolutely 
optimize our total water withdrawal.
3
2
Product-Level Impact: Greenfuel 
& Future Mobility
Our management of natural capital extends far beyond 
our factory walls and into the core DNA of the products we 
build. Through Lumax Greenfuel Energy Solutions, we are 
directly facilitating the national shift toward cleaner fuel 
platforms, acting as a critical enabler for OEMs looking to 
meet stringent BS-VI and upcoming emission norms.
4
By supplying high-pressure storage and delivery 
systems for CNG and Hydrogen and aggressively 
localizing components (such as ferrule-less tubes, which 
drastically reduce the risk of fugitive gas emissions 
while lowering overall vehicle weight), we are actively 
reducing the lifecycle emissions of the vehicles 
we equip.
With an unprecedented 40% of our order book now 
dedicated to future and clean mobility solutions, our 
product portfolio is a direct contributor to global climate 
action, fundamentally transforming our revenue mix 
toward sustainable, future-ready technologies.
Utilizing recycled and lower GSM invoice paper, 
alongside optimized invoice formats and digital 
registers, which cumulatively saves hundreds of 
trees annually.
Enforcing strict waste segregation, extensive material 
recycling and vermi-composting for food waste across 
our campuses, turning organic cafeteria waste into 
nutrient-rich manure for our green belts.
Reducing and reusing polybags and implementing 
standardized, durable packing bins for inbound 
and outbound logistics to eliminate single-use 
transit plastics.

Health, Safety and Employee Well-being
The Company has deeply embedded an Occupational Health and Safety Management System as a core component of 
its operations. As of FY 2025-26, 97.44% Safety Protocols of our plants are ISO 45001 certified (increased from 85.19% in 
FY 2024–25).
Safety Protocols
Hazard Identification and Risk 
Assessment (HIRA) exercises are 
conducted continuously across all 
facilities, governed daily by a stringent 
188-point Safety Audit Checklist. For non-
routine or high-risk tasks, a strict Permit-
to-Work system is enforced.
Comprehensive Wellbeing
We provide extensive on-site care through 
Occupational Health Centres and in-house doctors 
and nursing staff for medical consultations and 
emergency care. Our comprehensive benefits 
package includes Provident Fund coverage, extensive 
health insurance for employees and their families, 
gratuity and life insurance with compensatory support 
for families of deceased employees.
Training and Development for the Future
Technical skill development tailored to individual verticals took center stage in FY 2025–26. Alongside rigorous training in 
health, safety, quality and behavioral competencies, we expanded programs to include ESG awareness, GHG accounting, 
ISO 50001 protocols, AI tools and software fundamentals to equip our workforce to lead LATL’s  progress with positivity, 
confidence and capability.

Education: From Access to Empowerment
The classrooms of today shape the workforce and citizens of 
tomorrow.
LATL’s education initiatives are evolving from enabling access to 
actively shaping future-ready individuals.
The Girl Child Education program continues to address inherent 
gender disparities, reinforcing the Company’s belief that educating 
girls creates multi-generational impact. When a girl stays in school, 
the impact extends far beyond her own future to her home, her 
community and the nation.
Complementing this, Sunehra Kal equips students with critical life 
skills, fostering resilience, informed decision-making and social 
awareness. It focuses on the 10 core life skills identified by the 
World Health Organisation (WHO), equipping students across 
Haryana, Maharashtra and Gujarat with tools to navigate both 
education and life.  This program helps in reducing dropout rates, 
curbing early marriages and preparing them to become informed, 
empowered citizens. In parallel, life skills and STEAM education 
(Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts and Mathematics) are 
being integrated into primary schools in Haryana and Uttarakhand, 
strengthening foundational learning and nurturing curiosity from an 
early age.
Recognizing the growing importance of Digital Literacy, the 
initiative bridges the technology divide, ensuring that students 
from underserved communities are equipped for an increasingly 
digital world. The program places trained computer teachers in 
government schools where labs remain underutilized due to the 
lack of qualified instructors. By providing trained professionals to 
bridge this gap, we enable eager students to access digital literacy. 
Through Career Margdarshan, we address a crucial gap in rural 
education ecosystems, providing clarity, direction and confidence 
to young individuals navigating career choices. Pre-assessment 
tests, career guidance, one-on-one counselling and psychometric 
assessments help students align their capacity with their interests 
and raise awareness of vocational and skill-based options.  
The program also prepares students for competitive entrance 
examinations - CUET.
Similarly, the ‘Usha Ki Kiran’ Scholarship Program removes financial 
barriers, enabling deserving students including ‘persons with 
disabilities’ to pursue education, taking a step towards inclusive 
higher education.
The  investment in personal and menstrual hygiene awareness 
has strengthened and improved attendance and fostered dignity 
among students. By addressing stigma and misinformation around 
adolescence and menstrual health, the program has created safer, 
more empowered school communities.
In line with government directives to focus on aspirational districts, 
the Company has been active in Nuh - Mewat, Haryana. A sanitary 
pad manufacturing unit has been set up in the village to fulfil the 
need to supply free of cost sanitary pads to the students of the 
menstrual hygiene program. This is led by rural women advancing 
both public health and women empowerment. Women are trained in 
production, distribution and sales, fostering financial independence 
and empowerment. 
School infrastructure including toilets, classrooms etc., provides 
a conducive environment that encourages learning, improves 
attendance and community pride.
Skilling: Enabling Economic Independence
Recognising that sustainable development requires economic 
empowerment, LATL has expanded its focus on skill-building.
Launched in partnership with the  Automotive Skill Development, 
the program Saksham Safalta is a significant step towards 
industry-aligned skilling. By equipping youth with practical training, 
certification and placement support, the program creates direct 
pathways to employment and financial independence. In its 
inaugural year, the program is equipping young people with the 
skills and credentials to build real careers.
This marks a clear progression UpSHIFT, from only education to 
skilling and employability ensuring that beneficiaries are not just 
skilled, but industry-ready.

Governance
The Governance Framework 
Enabling Sustainable Growth.
Scaling operations, integrating global technologies and entering new domains 
such as software and embedded electronics all require a governance framework 
that can keep pace with the complexity of the decisions being made.
At LATL, governance is not a compliance layer that sits alongside the business. It is the framework within which the BRIDGE strategy is 
executed: providing the discipline that ensures structural ambition is matched by operational integrity, risk awareness and transparent 
accountability to all stakeholders.
Board of Directors: A Confluence of Expertise
Our Board of Directors is the ultimate custodian of our 
strategic vision. To guide our pivot toward intelligent 
mobility and complex systems integration, we have 
intentionally curated a Board that blends deep automotive 
legacy with advanced financial, technological and 
strategic acumen.
1
Independence & Objectivity 
The Board comprises 50% Independent Directors, 
ensuring unbiased oversight and independent 
evaluation of management performance.
Diversity of Thought 
We maintain boardroom diversity, with 12.5% female 
representation and a broad spectrum of industry 
expertise spanning global joint venture management, 
digital transformation and sustainable finance.
Strategic Oversight 
In FY 2025-26, the Board played a highly active role in 
approving and monitoring critical capital allocations, the 
strategic land acquisitions and the establishment of the 
SHIFT tech centre in Bengaluru.
Ethical Business Conduct and Compliance
Operational excellence is impossible without absolute 
integrity. Our governance framework is operationalized 
daily through strict, zero-tolerance policies that govern the 
behavior of every employee, supplier and partner.
2
Code of Conduct 
A comprehensive Code of Conduct mandates fair 
competition, anti-bribery and anti-corruption practices 
across all LATL entities and joint ventures.
Whistle-Blower Mechanism 
We maintain a secure, anonymous vigil mechanism, 
empowering employees and value-chain partners to 
report unethical conduct without fear of retaliation.
Regulatory Agility 
The Board ensures that LATL stays ahead of the 
regulatory curve, maintaining full compliance with 
the New Labour Code, advanced BRSR (Business 
Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting) mandates 
and evolving automotive safety standards.

ESG Governance: Sustainability as a Board 
Mandate
Our commitment to decoupling operational growth from 
environmental impact is driven directly from the top. The 
CSR & ESG Committee of the Board holds the ultimate 
responsibility for our sustainability trajectory.
4
Target Setting & Accountability 
The Board reviews and approves our ambitious 
targets for Scope 1 and Scope 2 emission reductions, 
water neutrality (ZLD) and our zero-waste-to-
landfill commitments.
Monitoring the Clean Mobility Shift 
The Board actively tracks the revenue contribution 
from our green mobility portfolio (including Greenfuel 
and EV components), ensuring that our capital 
allocation directly supports the transition to sustainable 
automotive ecosystems.
Enterprise Risk Management (ERM): 
Navigating New Horizons
As our product portfolio evolves from mechanical hardware 
to software-defined and connected systems, our risk 
horizon fundamentally expands. Our Board-led Risk 
Management Committee has upgraded our ERM framework 
to proactively identify and mitigate the unique risks 
associated with our technological leap.
3
Cybersecurity & Data Privacy 
Lumax has strengthened its IT structure with multi-
layered security systems including Antivirus, EDR, 
Zero Trust architecture and Data Leakage Protection, 
supported by ISO 27001 and TISAX certifications. 
Continuous phishing awareness training ensures 
employee vigilance. Our hybrid IT strategy leverages 
secure cloud and SaaS platforms such as SAP 
Rise alongside in-house systems for plant-specific 
data. With SAP Rise guaranteeing 99.7% uptime 
and fragmented multi-location data storage, 
our disaster recovery and business continuity 
framework ensures resilience, cost optimization and 
uninterrupted protection of core manufacturing and 
ERP operations.
Intellectual Property (IP) Protection 
As we localize advanced technologies and co-create 
proprietary solutions with our 6 global JV partners, 
the Board oversees strict IP protection protocols to 
safeguard our competitive moat.
Supply Chain Resilience 
The Board continuously monitors geopolitical and 
logistical risks, guiding our strategy to localize critical 
components (like CNG ferrule-less tubes) and maintain a 
highly diversified, domestic supplier ecosystem.
Climate Risk Integration 
Environmental risks are now systematically integrated 
into our ERM matrix, ensuring our operations remain 
resilient against climate-related disruptions and aligned 
with evolving emissions regulations.

II. S TATE OF COMPANY’S AFFAIRS
  The Indian automotive industry witnessed a year of 
robust growth during the financial year under review. 
While the passenger vehicle (PV) segment continued 
its growth trajectory, supported by healthy consumer 
demand and increased production, the two-wheeler 
(2W) segment also recorded robust growth. Leveraging 
its diversified product portfolio, successful introduction 
of new products, and the continued confidence 
of Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), the 
Company delivered consolidated growth that exceeded 
the overall industry growth rate.
  The year mark ed another significant milestone in the 
Company’s growth journey. Expansion of the product 
portfolio, coupled with increased business from 
existing customers, contributed to improved revenue 
performance and further strengthened the Company’s 
market position.
  R ecognizing the growing emphasis by OEMs 
on localization and supply chain resilience, the 
Company continued to invest in the modernization 
and upgradation of its manufacturing facilities. These 
strategic investments will enhance the Company’s 
capability to localize technologically advanced 
products, strengthen operational efficiencies, and 
provide customers with high-quality, reliable and  
cost-effective solutions while mitigating supply chain risks.
  The Company remains focused on increasing its 
presence in the passenger vehicle segment, which 
continues to offer significant long-term growth 
opportunities. Through its various joint ventures and 
subsidiaries, the Company is expanding its portfolio with 
future-ready technologies and advanced product lines 
to address evolving customer requirements. These 
strategic initiatives are expected to further strengthen 
the Company’s competitive positioning, deepen 
customer relationships, and support sustainable long-
term growth.
  The Company’ s continued focus on operational 
excellence, technology enhancement, localization, 
and customer-centric innovation positions it well to 
capitalize on emerging opportunities in the evolving 
automotive landscape and create long-term value for 
all stakeholders.
  The Company stands as a leading integrated automotive 
component manufacturer in India, with a diversified 
portfolio spanning advanced plastics, mechatronics, 
BOARD’S REPORT (Contd.)

--- page 75 ---
Lumax Auto Technologies Limited
72
structures & control systems, aftermarket solutions and 
alternate fuel systems.
  With over four decades of operational excellence, the 
Company has transitioned from a traditional component 
supplier to a system-level solution provider, driven by 
increasing content per vehicle (CPV), premiumization 
trends and deeper integration with OEM platforms.
 Business Segments
 Advanced Plastics & Interior S ystems
  The Company’ s largest business segment, Advanced 
Plastics & Interior Systems, continued to drive revenue 
growth, supported by strong demand from passenger 
vehicle platforms and increasing premiumization. The 
segment comprises interior modules, blow-moulded and 
injection-moulded components, and high-value plastic 
assemblies. The integration of IAC India has strengthened 
scale, customer engagement and profitability, while 
higher CPV continues to support growth.
 S tructures & Control Systems
  This segment includes gear shifters, metallic 
assemblies and control systems. Growth was driven by 
increasing adoption of automatic transmission systems, 
portfolio expansion into higher-value products and 
export opportunities through joint venture partnerships. 
Strong OEM relationships continue to support steady 
performance.
 Aftermarket
  The aftermark et business remained a stable and high-
margin segment, supported by a strong distribution 
network and established brands. Growth was driven 
by channel expansion, portfolio enhancement and 
improved market reach across replacement parts and 
automotive components.
 Mechatronics
  The Mechatronics business continued to gain 
momentum, driven by increasing demand for 
connected and intelligent vehicle technologies. New 
product launches, commencement of production 
across subsidiaries/joint ventures and a healthy order 
book are expected to support meaningful revenue and 
margin growth over the medium term.
 Alternate Fuel S ystems
  The Alternate Fuel S ystems business, led by LGESPL, 
continued to expand, supported by rising adoption of 
CNG and LNG vehicles, favorable regulatory trends 
and localization initiatives. The Company is focused on 
broadening its product portfolio and increasing CPV.
 Others
  The “ Others” segment comprises legacy and 
smaller businesses, including lighting and diversified 
automotive components. While modest in scale, these 
businesses continue to provide stable revenues and 
support portfolio diversification.
 T echnology Centre
  The Company strengthened its innovation capabilities  
through its Bengaluru-based Technology Centre, SHIFT 
(Smart Hub for Innovation and Future Trends). The 
center focuses on electronics, digital systems and next-
generation mobility solutions, supporting the Company’s 
transition towards a system-level solutions provider.
 Global Expansion
  During the year , the Company established its 
representative office in China. The office focuses on 
technology benchmarking, sourcing and tooling, while 
facilitating technology partnerships and supporting 
new business opportunities. It will operate in close 
collaboration with the SHIFT Technology Centre 
in Bengaluru to accelerate innovation and product 
development.
 Manufacturing Initiatives
  The Company continued to strengthen its manufacturing 
footprint through strategic land acquisitions in Gujarat 
during FY 2025-26, following its investment in the 
Kharkhoda region of Haryana in FY 2024-25. These 
investments will enhance manufacturing capacity, 
supply chain readiness and proximity to key customers, 
supporting future growth.
  During this year , the Company’s strategic focus has been 
strongly aligned towards strengthening cybersecurity, 
accelerating AI adoption, and driving end-to-end 
digitalization across the organization. As part of this 
journey, Company upgraded its Google Workspace 
environment from Business to Enterprise, enabling 
advanced security features along with integrated AI 
capabilities through Gemini. This enhancement is 
empowering the teams with improved productivity, 
smarter collaboration and a more intelligent digital 
workplace experience.
  In parallel, Company has launched the DO JO 2.0 
initiative as a pilot project on select machines, focusing 
on enhancing operational excellence, standardization 
and continuous improvement practices. Based on the 
outcomes and learnings from this pilot, Company plans 
to roll out DOJO 2.0 in a phased manner across all 
plants to drive consistency, efficiency and productivity 
improvements at an enterprise level.

governance processes. The evaluation considered 
the balance of skills, experience, independence 
and knowledge of the management and the 
Board, its overall diversity, and analysis of the 
Board and its Directors’ functioning.
  EVALUATION TECHNIQUE
		• 	 	The evaluation methodology involves 
completion of questionnaires consisting of 
certain parameters such as Evaluation factor, 
Ratings and Comments, if any.
		• 	 	The performance of entire Board is evaluated 
by all the Directors based on Board 
composition and quality, Board meetings 
and procedures, Board development, Board 
strategy and risk management etc.
		• 	 	The performance of the Managing Director 
and Executive Directors is evaluated by all 
the Board Members based on factors such 
as leadership, strategy formulation, strategy 
execution, external relations etc.
		• 	 	The performance of Non-Executive Director 
and Independent Directors is evaluated by 
other Board Members based on criteria like 
managing relationship, knowledge and skill, 
personal attributes, independence from the 
management etc.
		• 	 	It also involves self-assessment by all the 
Directors and evaluation of Committees 
of Board based on knowledge, diligence

 C.   CODE OF CONDUCT TO REGULATE, MONITOR 
AND REPORT TRADING BY DESIGNATED 
PERSONS (CODE OF CONDUCT)
   In compliance with the provisions of R egulation 9 of 
Securities and Exchange Board of India (Prohibition 
of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, the Company 
has adopted a Code of Conduct to regulate, monitor 
and report trading by Designated Persons. This 
Code of Conduct is intended to prevent misuse of 
Unpublished Price Sensitive Information (“UPSI”) by 
designated persons and also includes a Policy and 
Procedure for Inquiry in case of leakage of UPSI or 
suspected leakage of UPSI.
   The said Code provides guidelines advising 
Designated Persons on the procedures to follow 
and disclosures to make when dealing with the 
Company’s shares, while also warning them 
about the consequences of non-compliance. The 
Company has Code of Practices and Procedures 
for fair disclosure of unpublished price-sensitive 
information which includes a policy for determining 
legitimate purposes.
   Furthermore , the Company has established 
an adequate and effective system of internal 
controls and standardized processes to ensure 
compliance with these regulations and to prevent 
insider trading.
   Any violations of the Code are dealt with strictly in 
accordance with applicable regulatory provisions 
and the Company’s Code of Conduct, reinforcing a 
zero-tolerance approach towards insider trading.
   During the financial year under review, the 
Company identified three (3) cases in violation 
of the said code and the same were reported to 
the Audit Committee for necessary action. The 
Committee directed the concerned designated 
persons to disgorge the profits made to the Investor 
Protection and Education Fund (IPEF) of the SEBI 
and also issued a guidance to exercise abundant 
caution and ensure compliance with the Code. The 
intimations in this regard were duly submitted by 
the Company to the Stock Exchanges.
   CODE OF CONDUCT FOR DIRECT ORS AND 
SENIOR MANAGEMENT OF THE COMPANY
   The Company has adopted a Code of Conduct 
for its Directors and Senior Management, which 
is available on the Company’s website at https://

latl_code-of-conduct-for-directors-and-senior-

VI.  CORPORA TE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY (CSR) 
POLICY AND INITIATIVES
  The Company is dedicated to continuing to give 
back to society while expanding and conducting its 
business in a socially responsible and sustainable 
manner. A judiciously planned CSR program improves 
and influences communities by generating social and 
environmental value. The Company’s primary areas of 
focus continue to be “Quality Education” and “Good 
Health” for underprivileged sections of society, in line 
with the areas covered under Schedule VII and the 
Sustainable Development Goals.
  During the year , the Company continued its support 
to existing educational institutions by offering career 
counselling and guidance integrating students into 
mainstream schools, providing books and other 
learning resources, life-skills and soft skills training, 
expanding opportunities for a holistic education.
  As part of its health initiatives, the Company continues 
to focus on preventive healthcare through regular 
health check-up camps for cataract surgeries and by 
providing financial support to children suffering from 
juvenile diabetes.
  L umax Charitable Foundation (“Foundation”), the 
Company’s CSR arm is principally responsible for 
carrying out the Company’s CSR projects, with a 
focus on providing healthcare and education to 
disadvantaged communities.
  In compliance with the provisions of the Act, the 
Company has constituted a CSR Committee of the 
Board and has instituted and implemented a CSR Policy. 
The Committee monitors and oversees the Company’s 
various CSR projects and initiatives.
  During the year under review , the Company’s obligation 
to spend on the CSR activities was ` 376.80 Lakhs  
[` 368.62 Lakhs (after set-off)] i.e. 2% of the average net 
profits during the three immediately preceding financial 
years against which the Company has actually spent  
` 377.33 Lakhs including the administrative expenses.
  Consequent to the scheme(s) of merger of L umax 
Ancillary Limited (LAL) and IAC International Automotive 
India Private Limited (IAC India) with the Company, the 
CSR expenditure made by LAL and IAC India during 
the FY 2025-26 has been clubbed and reported along 
with the CSR expenditure done by the Company for  
FY 2025-26.
 KEY CSR A CTIVITIES
  As part of its commitment to the SDGs of Quality 
Education and Good Health, the Company offers 
holistic education opportunities as well as preventive 
and curative health initiatives, overseen by the Lumax 
Charitable Foundation team and its implementation 
partners.
 EDUCATION
  With the aim of delivering holistic and quality 
education, the Foundation’s interventions include 
girl child enrolment in schools, learning aids and 
beyond-school learning support. The goal is to enable 
underprivileged students to enhance their learning 
experience through continuous life-skills and soft-skills 
training, comprehensive career counselling and field 
excursion trips. The programs also assist in providing 
scholarships to students to continue their education 
without disruption due to financial constraints.
  Continuous infrastructure support is provided to 
government schools, including construction of toilets 
and classrooms, wall painting and other infrastructure 
work, to ensure a conducive environment at school. 
These programs are conducted preferably in the 
vicinity of the Company’s plant locations.
  During the year , the Company also initiated a skill 
development program in association with the 
BOARD’S REPORT (Contd.)

--- page 85 ---
Lumax Auto Technologies Limited
82
Automotive Skills Development Council (ASDC), 
aimed at enhancing the employability and technical 
competence of youth from the communities around its 
operations.
 HEALTH
  Under health interventions, the Foundation has 
organized eye care camps, conducting eye 
examinations and cataract procedures and supporting 
children with juvenile diabetes.
  The Foundation also supports the treatment of cancer 
patients and helps in covering gaps in cancer care for 
outstation children coming to Delhi / NCR for treatment, 
including gaps in nutrition, education, mental health 
care/counselling, lodging etc.
  During the year, the Company also launched Mobile 
Health Units, aimed at bringing primary healthcare 
services at the doorsteps of underserved and needy 
communities, thereby improving last-mile access to 
essential health services.

ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
Global Economy
The global economy entered FY 2025-26 amidst a complex 
macroeconomic environment characterized by evolving 
trade dynamics, geopolitical uncertainties and elevated 
interest rates. While growth remained resilient across several 
major economies, heightened energy prices and supply 
chain disruptions continued to influence global economic 
activity. However, the outbreak of conflict in the Middle 
East during the second half of the year materially altered 
the outlook. The International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its  
April 2026 World Economic Outlook, projected global growth 
at 3.1% in CY 2026 and 3.2% in CY 2027, a moderation from 
the 3.4% growth recorded during CY 2025. This reflects 
the pressures of elevated energy prices, tighter financial 
conditions and weakened business sentiment; however 
AI-led productivity gains and resilient private consumption 
provide partial offsets.1
Global headline inflation, which had been on a steady 
decreasing path, is projected to edge up to 4.4% in CY 2026 
before resuming its decline in CY 2027, driven largely by 
the pass-through of higher crude prices, freight costs and 
commodity-linked input pressures. Advanced economies 
have seen modest downward growth revisions, while 
commodity-importing emerging markets, particularly in Asia 
and Sub-Saharan Africa, face more pronounced adjustments. 
Growth in the United States is expected to moderate as 
residual tariff effects work through supply chains, while the 
Eurozone remains range-bound with growth projected in the 
1.0-1.2% corridor.2
Trade dynamics remain a defining feature of the global 
landscape. The interim US-India trade agreement concluded 
earlier in CY 2026, which reduced effective tariffs to 
18% from earlier proposed levels of 50%, has provided 
partial relief to export-oriented sectors. Progress on the  
India-EU Free Trade Agreement is expected to further 
improve market access over the medium term. 3 For the 
automotive and auto component value chain, these 
developments carry meaningful implications: supply chains 
are being reconfigured around diversification strategies, 
critical raw material flows (including rare-earth magnets 
and specialty electronics) remain concentrated and freight 
corridors around the Strait of Hormuz have become a key 
watch-item for cost visibility. The IMF highlights that the 
outlook remains highly contingent on the duration and 
intensity of the Middle East conflict, with downside scenarios 
implying materially lower global growth.

For automotive and auto component manufacturers, the 
read-through is two-fold. On the cost side, firmer crude 
oil, logistics and commodity prices exert pressure on input 
margins, particularly for import-linked components. On the 
demand side, resilient consumption in key Asian markets 
and the gradual easing of tariffs support export opportunities, 
while the accelerating shift to electrification and software-
defined vehicles continues to reshape the component mix.
Indian Economy
India remained one of the fastest-growing major economies 
globally during FY 2025-26, with the Reserve Bank of India 
(RBI) maintaining real GDP growth at 7.6% for FY 2025-26, 
supported by robust domestic demand, strong manufacturing 
momentum and a resilient services sector. GDP growth 
reported at 8.4% in Q2 FY 2025-26 and moderated to 7.8% in 
Q3 FY 2025-26, reflecting sustained economic momentum 
despite a high base and post-festive normalization. Growth 
remained predominantly domestically driven, with private 
consumption and government capital expenditure continuing 
to anchor economic activity during the year. For FY 2026-27, 
the central bank has estimated growth at 6.9%, indicating a 
calibrated moderation amid evolving global uncertainties, 
including geopolitical risks and energy price volatility.4

Outlook
The Indian economy is expected to sustain its growth 
momentum through FY 2026-27, supported by strong 
domestic fundamentals. Private consumption is expected to 
strengthen further, supported by stable inflation, improving 
income visibility and a resilient labor market. Investment 
activity is likely to accelerate on the back of higher capacity 
utilization in manufacturing, a healthier corporate balance 
sheet and continuing public capital expenditure. Export 
growth, while subject to global trade realignments, remains 
supported by improving competitiveness and widening 
market access.
The principal downside risks relate to geopolitical 
fragmentation, prolonged elevation in crude oil prices and 
currency volatility. For discretionary categories including 
automobiles, however, supportive policy measures, stable 
financing conditions and tax adjustments continue to provide 
a favorable demand environment which is expected to 
support demand conditions through FY 2026-27.
AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Global Automotive Industry
Global light-vehicle sales rose 3.4% in CY 2025 to 91.7 Million 
units, the first year to exceed the CY 2019 pre-COVID peak 
of 89.9 Million and S&P Global Mobility expects 2026 sales 
to remain near-flat at 91.8 Million units, with global production 
ticking down 0.4% to 92.6 Million.7
Production outlook has been revised across key regions, 
reflecting demand softness, geopolitical disruptions and 
affordability pressures. In the United States, CY 2026 and  
CY 2027 production are now estimated at 14.3 Million (1.5%) 
and 15.3 Million (2.3%), with further cuts due to conflict spill-
overs and weakening demand; while OEMs are initially 
absorbing tariff impacts 8, gradual price increases are 
expected amid already elevated vehicle prices. In Europe, 
CY 2026 production has also been trimmed due to energy 
costs and affordability constraints, with Germany still below 
pre-COVID levels and France lagging, as OEMs navigate 
electrification mandates, rising Chinese EV competition 
and a consumer shift toward hybrids. In China, domestic 
demand remains subdued due to lower subsidies and weak 
sentiment, leading to downward revisions, although exports 
continue to provide structural support. Meanwhile, Japan 
and Korea have seen modest cuts, with Japanese OEMs 
benefiting from a weaker yen and evolving supply chain 
strategies, including increased localized and sourcing shifts.
A key structural shift is that Chinese-origin brands now 
account for 26.5% of global vehicle production (24.8 Million 
units, +18% Y o Y in CY 2025) and are projected to take 27.4% 
in CY 2026 7. More tellingly, Chinese OEMs’ production 
outside China grew from 1.1 Million units in CY 2025 to a 
forecast 1.6 Million in CY 2026, a 45% increase that signals 
the second wave of the Chinese auto export thrust: localised 
manufacturing in Europe, Southeast Asia, Mexico and Egypt.
Another key trend is the moderation of pure-Battery Electric 
Vehicle (BEV) adoption in favor of a multi-powertrain world. 
S&P Global Mobility now projects electrified vehicles (BEV

OEMs are caught between three forces in CY 2026: (i) tariff

aggressive value propositions. As a result: OEMs globally 
are recalibrating product portfolio and investment priorities 
to balance profitability, affordability and electrification 
objectives.
Software-defined vehicles (SDVs) represent a key medium-
term margin lever. Recurring software/services revenue, 
OTA-update monetization and ADAS feature unlocks are 
reshaping the OEM business model.
Global Auto Component Industry
The global auto components industry, estimated at ~USD  
1.8-2.0 Trillion in revenue, is in the middle of its most 
significant restructuring since the 1980s. Three forces 
converge: (i) the EV content uplift (BEVs require ~3-4x the 
value of power electronics, motors, battery management and 
thermal management vs ICE); (ii) software-and-electronics 
share rising to 30%+ of vehicle BoM by 2030; and (iii) the 
collapse of legacy ICE-only supplier economics as volumes 
for engines, fuel systems and exhaust components face 
structural decline. Tier-1 suppliers globally are bifurcating 
into ‘EV-ready’ and ‘value migrants’ exiting ICE-dependent 
product lines.

The Indian auto industry posted its strongest fiscal year in 
seven years (since FY 19), with production of 34.71 Million units, 
up 12.0% Y o Y and robust performance across segments.1112

Indian Auto Component Industry
The Indian auto components industry is now a USD 80+ 
billion-revenue industry at annualized pace, reflecting strong 
OEM growth, an expanding vehicle parc (number of vehicles 
on the road) and the formalization of repair and maintenance 
channels. The PLI architecture is specifically designed to 
deepen India from ‘assembly-driven’ to ‘vertically integrated’. 
The 12.5% Y o Y growth in component imports (driven primarily 
by China) is flipping the trade balance from a USD 150 Million 
surplus to a USD 180 Million deficit reveals the uncomfortable 
truth about India’s auto-components positioning: even as India 
exports more, it is also importing more sophisticated sub-
systems (rare-earth magnets, power electronics, EV-specific 
components) from China. ACMA leadership has explicitly 
flagged securing critical materials, including rare-earth 
magnets, as the top supply-chain priority for FY 2026-27. 15 
Dependence on imports of certain advanced components 
and critical materials, including rare earth magnets and 
power electronics, remains a key strategic consideration for 
the industry. This also presents opportunities for localisation 
and domestic value addition.
OPPORTUNITIES
Expanding Domestic Vehicle Demand
The expanding middle class and rapid urbanization are 
fuelling a surge in automobile demand. This, in turn, is 
propelling growth in the auto component sector. The growth 
of India’s middle class is leading to higher vehicle ownership, 
driven by rising incomes, better education, and employment 
opportunities. These factors boost disposable income and 
encourage spending on personal transportation. 
Premiumization
ASP-led growth now contributes more to industry revenue 
than unit-volume growth in most quarters. The component 
implication: precision engineering, ADAS, infotainment, 
premium interiors and lighting are the highest-growth sub-
verticals, far ahead of generic body-and-chassis components.
Software, Electronics and the SDV Transition
The vehicle BoM is shifting from majority mechanical to more 
electronics- and software-led in the next few years. India’s 
strength in software, embedded systems and engineering 
services is structurally aligned with this shift. The global 
engineering-R&D services opportunity for Indian auto-
services firms is expected to be in the USD 50-60 Billion 
range by CY 2028.
Emergence as a Global Sourcing Hub 
India is being considered a potential global automotive supply 
chain alternative under global diversification strategy. This 
strategy encourages companies to diversify manufacturing 
beyond China. Additionally, India’s automotive industry is 
gaining importance in global supply chains due to strategic 
localization, economic growth, endurance, and targeted 
investments in infrastructure and technology. 
Technological Advancements 
India is enhancing its advanced manufacturing infrastructure 
through increased foreign direct investment and a focus 
on localizing advanced components to reduce import 
dependency. The country is also embracing advanced 
technologies like robotics, automation, and Industry 4.0 
to improve productivity and meet international quality 
standards, positioning itself as a competitive player. 
Aftermarket - The Under-Appreciated Structural 
Compounder
With the strong increase in vehicle parc, the aftermarket is 
the single most predictable growth pool in the industry for 
the next decade, with relatively higher margin profile. The 
formalization tailwind such as growing organized channels 
compounds the secular volume growth.
THREATS 
Supply Chain Disruptions 
The sector contends with geopolitical and economic 
disruptions, prompting the need to localize critical

components to reduce import dependency, especially from 
China. Logistics challenges are exacerbated by geopolitical 
tensions, complicating and raising input and transportation 
costs. As a result, the sector remains vulnerable to global 
supply chain disruptions and currency fluctuations due to 
significant reliance on imported advanced components. 
Transition to EVs 
The shift to EVs presents both challenges and opportunities 
for the auto component industry. While EV adoption is 
accelerating, it poses significant threats to traditional 
auto component manufacturers due to the fundamental 
change in vehicle architecture. The demand for ICE-related 
components, such as engines, transmissions, and fuel 
systems is expected to decline, impacting businesses that 
rely heavily on these parts. Additionally, developing skills for 
EV production remains a challenge, as the existing workforce 
may not be adequately trained for battery technology, 
power electronics, and electric drivetrains. Moreover, the 
growth of the EV segment is highly dependent on charging 
infrastructure, battery supply chains, and government 
incentives. 
Margin Pressure from OEMs
OEMs, facing their own margin squeeze, are pushing 
component pricing down by 2-4% annually in real terms. 
Sustainable defence for component manufacturers is 
technology differentiation, cost-leadership through scale 
and efficiency enhancements. 
Government Regulations and Compliance 
The auto component industry faces uncertainty and increased 
production costs due to constantly changing government 
policies and regulations, as manufacturers adapt to new 
emissions and safety standards. Evolving labor regulations, 
including the implementation of new labor codes and  
state-specific requirements may necessitate changes 
to workforce policies, payroll structures, contractor 
management and compliance processes, resulting in higher 
administrative costs and operational complexity.
Demand Slowdown In Developed Markets
US, Europe and Japan together account for 50% of global 
auto demand by value and 60% of auto-component import 
value. Any combination of (i) Fed reaction-function tightening, 
(ii) European recession, or (iii) Japanese yen-driven import 
compression hits Indian auto exports through volume and 
price simultaneously.
Geopolitical Risks
Geopolitical risks, including changes in tariff structures, 
regional conflicts, trade restrictions, and supply chain 
disruptions across key markets, may impact the global 
business environment. Such developments could result 
in volatility in commodity prices, logistics costs, currency 
movements, sourcing dynamics, and overall business 
continuity, potentially affecting operations and financial 
performance.
Company Overview 
Lumax Auto Technologies Limited (‘LATL’ or ‘the Company’) 
stands as a leading integrated automotive component 
manufacturer in India, with a diversified portfolio spanning 
advanced plastics, mechatronics, structures and control 
systems, aftermarket solutions and alternate fuel systems.
With over four decades of operational excellence, LATL 
has transitioned from a traditional component supplier to a 
system-level solution provider, driven by increasing content 
per vehicle (CPV), premiumization trends and deeper 
integration with OEM platforms.
The Company operates through a robust ecosystem of global 
partnerships and joint ventures, including collaborations with 
companies such as Mannoh, Cornaglia, IAC, Alps Alpine, 
Ituran, Jopp, FAE and Y okowo, enabling access to advanced 
technologies and enhancing product capabilities across 
segments. 
LATL has a strong manufacturing footprint of 28 facilities 
spread across Haryana, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, 
Maharashtra, Uttarakhand, Rajasthan and Karnataka across 
India and serves over 20 prominent customers in the 
automotive sector including leading OEMs such as M&M, 
Bajaj Auto, Maruti Suzuki, Tata Motors and HMSI.

CPV and premiumization trends across OEM platforms.

of ferrule-less tubes and fittings, positioning the Company

Risk Management
The Company has established a structured risk management framework to identify, assess and mitigate key business risks, 
ensuring long-term sustainability and resilience across its operations.
Risk Category Impact Mitigation Strategies
Economic Risk Slowdown in the automotive sector due to 
macroeconomic factors such as inflation, 
interest rates, global geopolitical instability 
or weak consumer demand could impact 
volumes.
Diversified customer base across OEMs and segments 
(PV, 2W, CV), increasing focus on the aftermarket business 
and expansion into export markets to reduce volatility.
Environmental 
Risk
The automotive industry contributes to air 
pollution, greenhouse gas emissions and 
impacts water resources and ecosystems.
Promoting sustainable mobility solutions: Using 
Greenfuel’s expertise in alternate fuel systems like CNG, 
LNG solutions. Enhancing fuel efficiency. Adopting 
sustainable manufacturing practices. Ensuring compliance 
with environmental standards. Implementing initiatives 
like Quality Control Circles (QCC), Total Productive 
Maintenance (TPM) and Lean Across the Company (LAC) 
to optimize production efficiency and reduce waste.
Competitive 
Disruption
Rapid technological shifts and intensified 
competition from EV-focused and low-cost 
global suppliers may reduce demand for 
traditional automotive components, resulting 
in revenue decline, margin pressure, 
and potential obsolescence of existing 
manufacturing capabilities.
The Company mitigates competitive disruption risk 
through portfolio diversification, investment in advanced 
technologies, strategic partnerships, operational 
excellence initiatives, customer diversification, and 
continuous capability enhancement.
Labor and Talent 
Risk
A shortage of skilled labor or workforce 
disputes can disrupt production and business 
operations.
Implementing robust talent acquisition and retention 
programs. Investing in training and development programs 
and fostering a positive work environment.
Supply Chain 
Risk
Disruptions due to natural calamities, 
geopolitical instability, or raw material 
shortages can delay production and increase 
costs.
Diversified sourcing strategy, localization of critical 
components, long-term supplier partnerships and 
continuous monitoring of supply chain risks.
Technological 
Risk
Accelerated pace of technological innovation 
may render existing products obsolete or 
reduce competitiveness.
Strong focus on R&D and innovation, establishment 
of technology centers (e.g., Bengaluru SHIFT) and 
collaborations with global technology partners.
Regulatory and 
Compliance Risk
Changes in emission norms, safety regulations 
and compliance requirements could increase 
costs or necessitate product redesign.
Continuous monitoring of regulatory developments, 
proactive product development aligned with future 
norms and adherence to global quality and compliance 
standards.
ESG and 
Sustainability 
Risk
Failure to meet evolving environmental, social, 
and governance expectations from regulators, 
OEMs, investors, and customers may result in 
increased compliance costs, loss of business 
opportunities, reputational damage, and 
reduced long-term competitiveness.
The Company mitigates ESG and sustainability risks 
through energy-efficient operations, responsible sourcing, 
strong governance practices, workforce safety initiatives, 
transparent ESG reporting, and long-term investments in 
sustainable manufacturing technologies.

CORPORATE GOVERNANCE REPORT
1. COMP ANY’S PHILOSOPHY ON CORPORATE 
GOVERNANCE
 The Corporate Governance philosophy at L umax Auto 
Technologies Limited (“LATL”/ “Lumax”/ “Company”) 
is anchored on the principles of transparency, 
accountability, and a steadfast commitment to long-
term sustainable growth.  LATL believes that robust 
governance is not merely a compliance requirement 
but a strategic tool to optimize the balance between 
stakeholder aspirations and corporate objectives.
 LA TL is dedicated to “doing things the right way”. This 
means the business decisions at LATL are consistently 
filtered through a lens of ethics and rigorous legal 
compliance. LATL regards its shareholders, employees, 
customers, and the community not just as beneficiaries, 
but as partners in its progress. By integrating global 
best practices with transparent disclosures, LATL 
ensures that its pursuit of solid financial results goes 
hand-in-hand with value creation for its stakeholders.
 LA TL governance framework provides a resilient 
foundation, ensuring timely and accurate communication 
regarding its performance and leadership. Beyond 
adhering to the Securities and Exchange Board of 
India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) 
Regulations, 2015 (“Listing Regulations”), LATL 
proactively evolves its internal standards to stay ahead 
of regulatory shifts and dynamic market environments, 
ensuring institutional stability in an ever-changing 
world.
 Empowerment through Board Leadership: Central to 
LATL’s philosophy is a dynamic and versatile Board of 
Directors. LATL believes that a diverse Board, bringing 
together a wealth of experience across different 
industries and geographies-is essential for effective 
oversight. LATL’s governance structure empowers the 
Board to provide visionary leadership while ensuring 
that management remains accountable to the highest 
standards of performance and integrity.
 Integrated Risk Management & Resilience:  In an 
era of global volatility, LATL views risk management 
as an integral component of Corporate Governance. 
LATL has institutionalized a framework that identifies, 
assesses, and mitigates risks-ranging from operational 
and financial to cyber and climate-related challenges. 
This proactive risk-culture ensures that LATL’s growth 
remains sustainable and its assets remain protected 
against unforeseen disruptions.
 Commitment to ESG and Ethical Value Creation: LATL 
recognizes that the long-term viability of its business is 
inextricably linked to the well-being of the planet and the 
communities it serves. Consequently, LATL’s governance 
model increasingly integrates Environmental, Social, 
and Governance (ESG) metrics into its core strategy. 
By fostering a culture of inclusivity, environmental 
stewardship, and ethical supply chain management, 
LATL aims to be a catalyst for positive change while 
delivering consistent, superior value to its shareholders.
 LA TL has complied with the requirements of Corporate

2. BO ARD OF DIRECTORS
 The Board of Directors serves as the core of the 
Company’s governance, acting as the ultimate custodian 
of shareholder interests and corporate integrity. This 
professional Board - comprising a balanced mix of 
Executive, Non-Executive and Independent Directors - 
provides the strategic vision and oversight necessary 
to navigate a complex business landscape. By critically 
evaluating management policies and the Company’s 
overall direction, the Board ensures that executive 
decisions align with the long-term goal of sustainable 
value creation while remaining responsive to immediate 
operational needs.
 Beyond its supervisory role , the Board is committed 
to fostering a culture of professional stewardship and 
accountability. It holds the primary responsibility for 
the general affairs and performance of the business, 
ensuring that management practices are both effective 
and ethically sound. Through rigorous evaluation and a 
focus on transparency, the Board maintains a resilient 
framework that protects the interests of all stakeholders, 
ensuring that the Company continues to operate with 
the highest standards of corporate citizenship and 
financial discipline.
 All statutory and other matters of significance including 
information as mentioned in the Part A of Schedule II to 
the Listing Regulations are complied with.

 (c)  Selection and Scheduling of Agenda Items for Board 
Meetings
 i)   The date of next Board Meeting is usually decided 
at the time of conclusion of Board Meeting.
 ii)   At least four Board Meetings are held in each 
financial year to review the quarterly results and 
additional Board Meetings are held on a need basis.
 iii)   The Company Secretary of the Company drafts 
and finalizes the agenda in consultation with the 
Chairman of the Company.
(i) Board Agenda
 Detailed Agenda and notes to Agenda are provided to  
the Directors in the defined Agenda format at least 7 days 
in advance of the meeting to align with the requirements 
under Secretarial Standard-1. All material information 
is incorporated in the agenda papers for facilitating 
meaningful and focused discussions at the Meeting. 
Where it is not practicable to attach any document 
to the agenda, the same is tabled before the Meeting 
with specific reference to this effect in the agenda. In 
special and exceptional circumstances, additional or 
supplementary item(s) on the agenda are permitted.
(ii) R ecording Minutes of proceedings at Board Meetings
 The Company Secretary records the Minutes of the 
proceedings of each Board and other Committees 
Meeting. Draft minutes are circulated within 15 days 
from the conclusion of the meeting to all the members 
of the Board / Committee for their comments. The final 
minutes are entered in the Minutes Book within 30 days 
from conclusion of the Meeting.
(iii) P ost Meeting Follow-up Mechanism
 The Guidelines for Board Meetings facilitate an effective  
post Meeting follow-up, review and reporting process for 
the decisions taken by the Board. The important decisions 
taken at the Board Meetings are communicated to the 
departments/divisions concerned promptly. Action taken 
report on the decisions/minutes of the previous Meeting(s) 
is placed at the immediately succeeding Meeting.

3. COMMITTEES OF THE BO ARD
 In terms of the Listing Regulations, the Board has 
constituted Five (5) Committees i.e.; Audit Committee, 
Nomination and Remuneration Committee, Corporate 
Social Responsibility Committee, Share Transfer/ 
Stakeholders’ Relationship Committee and Risk 
Management Committee.
 Every Committee has an important role to play within 
terms of its reference. The Committee Meetings are duly 
convened and held as considered appropriate from 
time to time. The process and procedure related to the 
Board Meetings are also applicable and followed for the 
Committee Meetings. The Chairperson of Committees 
provides a brief update about the discussions and 
recommendations of the Committee before the Board 
Meetings.
A. A udit Committee
 The Company has constituted A udit Committee in 
terms of Section 177 of the Act read with Regulation 18 
of the Listing Regulations, with the powers and roles 
assigned under applicable laws. The Committee acts 
as a link amongst the Management, Auditors and the 
Board. The Company Secretary of the Company acts as 
Secretary to the Audit Committee.
